chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Humran ibn A'yan from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who had the circumambulation of the women (Tawaf al-Nisa') upon him alone, so he circumambulated five of its paces, then his belly was pressed (by sexual urge), so he feared it would overtake him, so he went to his house, broke his state of Ihram, then had intercourse with his female slave. He said: 'He performs Ghusl, then returns and circumambulates the House two circumambulations to complete what remained of his circumambulation, and he seeks forgiveness from his Lord, and he does not return (to perform the rest of the Hajj rites).'

And if he had performed the circumambulation of the women and circumambulated three of its paces, then went out and had intercourse, then he has ruined his Hajj, and upon him is a camel, and he performs Ghusl, then returns and circumambulates a full week (seven circumambulations).'

And whoever has intercourse with his wife while he is in Ihram for an individual Umrah before he has finished its rituals, then his Umrah is invalidated, and upon him is a camel, and he remains in Mecca until the following month, then he completes his Umrah and departs if he wills. Narrated.

key_terms.أُسْبُوعاً: A full week, referring to seven complete circumambulations
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A camel, used as a specific form of expiation (kaffarah)
key_terms.طَوَافُ اَلنِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa', the final circumambulation of the Kaaba in Hajj
key_terms.عُمْرَةٍ مُفْرَدَةٍ: Individual Umrah, where the pilgrim remains in Ihram until completing all rites
key_terms.غَمَزَهُ بَطْنُهُ: His belly was pressed, a phrase indicating the onset of sexual urge

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim who breaks their Ihram due to sexual intercourse before completing the Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific expiations (*kaffarah*) for a pilgrim who engages in sexual intercourse while in the state of *Ihram*, distinguishing between breaking the state before or after completing *Tawaf al-Nisa'*. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a camel (*badanah*) as expiation and clarifies whether the Hajj is invalidated or merely requires completion, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the precise timing of the act relative to the ritual milestones. The ruling underscores the gravity of violating the sanctity of *Ihram* and the necessity of purification (*Ghusl*) and repentance (*Istighfar*) to restore ritual validity.
